column2: reason
Mechanical translation does not preserve the original ret 0x0c ABI; main-menu replay faults in its body at tick 695. Keep original bytes pending manual ABI recovery.
Mechanical body for this 5-byte JMP thunk is not ABI-equivalent; quick-fight bisector isolates it as sufficient for guest_exit at IP 0x222/tick 904. Keep original tail-jump bytes.

Cockpit replay bisector: compiled replacement causes unmapped fetch at IP 0x15918c05/tick 3188. Original bytes avoid the fetch but cockpit counters, framebuffer and guest RAM still diverge; leave original pending ABI/behavior fix.

Mechanical replacement loses the EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX plus two-stack-argument ABI; automatic M1 bisector identifies this entry alone as sufficient for the startup read fault. Keep original bytes pending manual recovery.
Mechanical GUI dispatch loop causes invalid instruction at IP 0x4df015 (tick 650); bisector isolates this entry. Keep original body pending hand recovery.

Focused menu-accept bisector: the mechanically compiled replacement is sufficient for an invalid-write path at guest address 0x19655800. Keeping original bytes reaches the instruction limit without a crash; RAM/framebuffer equivalence remains unresolved.
The guest DOS bridge delegates intdos to the original X-32 dispatcher to preserve its INT 21h path and unwritten carry-word quirk; patching this replacement would recurse.
The guest DOS bridge delegates int386x to the original X-32 interrupt thunk; patching this replacement would recurse and lose the original thunk behavior.

Original entry is a stack-preserving tail jump to 0x9c224; the C replacement trampoline pushes preserved registers ahead of its stack arguments and faults at 0x9c231 with a shifted selector. Keep the original JMP bytes.

M1 replay bisector isolates this replacement as sufficient for startup failure at INT 0 (IP 0x9c55a); keep the original flag-dependent interrupt-vector fragment until its DOS interrupt bridge is recovered.
Recovered dispatcher produces `ini: expected '='` while parsing extracted INIT3D.TXT and guest exits with code 0xff; keep original text-script dispatcher pending ABI/behavior recovery.

Original callers pass four stack arguments and expect ret 0x10. The compiled body reads Watcom register arguments and returns with plain ret, corrupting stack during logo setup; keep original bytes until a stack-aware ABI thunk is available.

Recovered loader causes `System.gui` line 1 to fail with `String "0" not recognised as a Variable`; original bytes remove the parser error and advance startup. Keep original pending behavioral recovery.
Original uses four register and four stack arguments and returns with ret 0x10. Current hybrid has no stack-aware trampoline for this ABI; restore original bytes pending support.

Original uses five caller-clean stack arguments. The recovered body expects four register arguments plus five stack arguments, producing a wrong buffer pointer during logo/menu drawing; keep original bytes.
Original uses five caller-clean stack arguments. The recovered body expects four register arguments plus five stack arguments; keep original bytes for ABI consistency with 0xeb050.

This is a threaded-dispatch tail-jump, not a returning helper: it selects and jumps to a record handler that returns to the caller. The C draft returns the handler address instead, so normalization skips the handler and corrupts the stream. Keep original dispatch bytes.

initialize_x32_services_e20 is a Linux-startup-probe reconstruction; as a hybrid redirect it faults on an unmapped read in the cockpit replay (bisect m2-bisect-002). Keep original pre-main X-32 setup.
Hybrid redirect breaks cockpit replay (bisect m2-bisect-003); keep original bytes.

Mechanical body drops the colour byte and three of four coordinates of each set_clip_rect_c94f4 call (bisect m2-bisect-009); keep original.
Mechanical body has uninitialised stack locals and guessed call args (bisect m2-bisect-010); keep original.
Mechanical body mis-scales uint32_t* array indices (bisect m2-bisect-011); keep original.
Mechanical body treats 64-bit float fields as uint64_t integers and guesses call args (bisect m2-bisect-012); keep original.
Hand wrapper forwards 11b134 without EAX object pointer and discards the st0 double result (bisect m2-bisect-013); fix signature, then re-enable.
Mechanical body guesses a uint64_t stack parameter and call args (bisect m2-bisect-014); keep original.
Bisect-implicated mechanical body (m2-bisect-015); stack-parameter ABI (param_1, param_2) unverified; keep original until reviewed.
